newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine firm rejects U.S. wheat, soybean offers.
newsitem.headline: Philippine firm rejects U.S. wheat, soybean offers.

text.p: A Philippine firm on Friday rejected offers for the supply of 23,000 tonnes U.S. wheat and 15,000 tonnes of soybeans due to high prices, traders said.
"The firm said it rejected all our offers due to high prices," a trader who joined the bidding told Reuters.
Executives of Philippine flour millers and other food companies said they have received offers to buy Canadian wheat and South American soybean.
"We are actually reviewing the offer for Canadian wheat and South American syobean due to high prices in the United States," said an official at a local flour miller.
Philippine firms buy most of their wheat and soybean requirements from the United States.
Canadian wheat suppliers have assured Philippine buyers that the port congestion in the port of Vancouver due to weather problems has eased.
Last month, Philippine mills that bought Canadian wheat for February and March deliveries sought price cuts from the suppliers due to delayed shipments.
